---
title: "After the session"
---
The session stops after the exploration of Task 4, and the exercise has one task more. Task 5 asks you to choose one specification, one option for each decision of the menu, and to fix it in the preregistration block of your report before you run it: the claim, the data-in-hand statement, your choices, a sentence from the causal graph on why the specification answers the claim, and your rule for what supports or undermines it. Render the report so that the block carries its date, then fit the specification with `run_spec()` and send it with `report_result()`, which draws it on the [class chart](../../cases/housing/multiverse.qmd#class-results) as a filled circle beside your exploratory mark. The [exercise overview](../../cases/housing/exercise.qmd) sets the task out in full, and the slides on preregistration in the [one-day deck](../../slides/housing-one-day.html#/part-4-multiverse-replication-and-preregistration){target="_blank"} explain what a preregistration settles and what it leaves open.

The [companion curriculum](../../companion/index.qmd) covers what the session could only mention in passing, in modules that each stand on their own.

| If you want | Read |
|---|---|
| The design of the experiment: random assignment, names as treatments, comparisons among replies, randomisation inference, power and the ethics of deception | [Audit experiments](../../companion/experiments.qmd) |
| Every model on the menu, from a difference in proportions to the logit, and how to read odds ratios against percentage points | [Binary outcomes](../../companion/binary-outcomes.qmd) |
| The causal graph of Task 2 at a slower pace, finished in the workspace | [Causal graphs and conditioning](../../companion/dags.qmd), with `R/dag_starter.R` in your workspace |
| The ideas behind the curve, and the arguments now being made against them | [The multiverse and its critics](../../companion/multiverse.qmd) |
| The replication with new data, in its own words and on its own data | The final report at [osf.io/2ug8x](https://osf.io/2ug8x/), and the de-identified data, the do-file and a dictionary at [osf.io/xseqg](https://osf.io/xseqg/) |
| R from the beginning, on the same data | [Getting started with R](../../companion/intro-r.qmd) |
| To archive and version the report that you wrote | [Reproducibility repositories](../../companion/repositories.qmd), then [Git and GitHub](../../companion/git-github.qmd) |

The [one-day course](../housing-one-day/index.qmd) takes the same case through the whole exercise, with the credibility debate, the toolchain, the estimand and the causal graph worked by hand, and the preregistration done together in class.
